[November 22, 2016. 1800 Hours.]

The Politburo Standing Committee was meeting, Wu Qiang at its head. It was his choice to meet. Something had been plaguing him… ever since that fateful day when he was 19 years old… June 4. Nobody here knew that – he had just been one in a sea of faces.

“The people already know about June 4,” Wu Qiang said, “There’s no reason to keep censoring something that everyone knows.” The other members of the Politburo Standing Committee were stone-faced. They knew as well as Wu Qiang that this was the case, but what would happen if the Party recognized it?

“We should take responsibility for the events of June 4,” Wu Qiang continued, “Even if you don’t agree with this, I will point out to you that our response to Tiananmen is the reason for the Arms Embargo by the West. This event nearly made us an international pariah. I think… it would be best if we finally recognized what happened on June 4, made amends to those still suffering from it. Not only do I think this is right, I think that this is a good move on the international stage. Let us not cling to denying what all already know.”

The Politburo Standing Committee was silent. These weren’t the same ones as Xi Jinping’s administration – most of them retired at 68, as they were supposed to. Tension was in the air. They couldn’t deny Wu Qiang’s points about the international effects, nor the common knowledge of the events, especially among the educated.

There were several words exchanged. Concerns raised. In the end, though, they were all pittances compared to Wu Qiang’s arguments.

“We will release those imprisoned for Tiananmen and discussion thereof, with a reparation of 100,000 Yuan per year imprisoned. For those we know died, we will give a reparation of 250,000 to their closest kin. What say you?” The Politburo Standing Committee discussed this, but they had already accepted Wu Qiang’s arguments. It was to be done.

“Very well. We have a lot of work to do. And much to admit… and announce.”

Excerpt

In some classrooms professors are asked to give “trigger alerts” when material is coming that might in some way be experienced as oppressive.

I believe this trend is anti-liberation.

I think it misses the point. The full quote continues

It further empowers power holders, asking authorities (in this case, teachers) to take even more responsibility to monitor and control. It disempowers those who have suffered oppression, by assuming they can’t stand up for themselves when an insult appears.

I think they're conflating two different notions of "trigger." There's the Tumblr definition of trigger, which is synonymous with insult. However, what many people are talking about are legitimate trauma triggers. Students with PTSD as a result of rape or abuse can be "triggered" by literature and experience the symptoms of PTSD when exposed to specific stimuli.

This is an instance where there is a legitimate concern, but overuse of the term by Tumblrinas has been regressive in the area, similar to how the DSM-recognized gender dysphoria has been made into a joke by people claiming they should be accepted as "Cat-kin"

We shouldn't think of "trigger" as "insult." We already have a word for that: "insult." And, no, we don't need to warn people that a book may insult them. However, if the book may genuinely cause victims of trauma to experience severe distress, then a warning may be appropriate.
